## 20/09/2026 19:55 — TestPulse V003 Review

Partner, I completed the **V003 deep review** across the uploaded codebase, sprint tracker, product workbook, handover and product-status material, plus current Atlassian documentation.

**Review workbook:**  
[Download chatgpt_review_V003_MoPr10-testpulse_atlassian_20260920_1955.xlsx](sandbox:/mnt/data/chatgpt_review_V003_MoPr10-testpulse_atlassian_20260920_1955.xlsx)

### Main conclusion

**Market demand:** **Yes at category level, but TestPulse-specific demand is still unproven.** The supplied material itself shows the missing primary validation/design-partner evidence. fileciteturn0file0L168-L173

**Enterprise grade:** **Not yet.** I would describe it as **enterprise-oriented engineering with insufficient enterprise operational evidence**. The codebase has become substantially stronger, but the product still lacks real Jira deployment evidence, real production performance, customer pilots, completed Marketplace purchase validation and external security assurance.

The supplied status is appropriately cautious: **66/95 planned tasks are done in code**, while live-site, human, procurement, purchase and decision dependencies remain. fileciteturn0file0L157-L167 It also explicitly states that operational evidence remains **1/10 because nothing has run on a real Jira site**. fileciteturn0file0L238-L241

I also independently executed the repository's **seven standing gates**. They all passed: reachability, claims, platform entrypoints, entrypoint wiring, scope/egress, secret/PII scan and concurrent-write safety. I did **not** claim an independent Jest pass: `npm test` could not start because the extracted environment had no installed Jest executable. That limitation is recorded in the workbook rather than being hidden.

### Important finding about AI / Runs on Atlassian

The source manifest declares `api.anthropic.com`. Current Atlassian documentation says Runs on Atlassian eligibility is based on the app's manifest/egress characteristics; apps generally cannot egress in-scope data to an external AI service and remain eligible. citeturn0search1turn0search3

So **turning AI off at runtime does not by itself make the current shipping manifest Runs-on-Atlassian eligible**. This should remain an explicit product/edition decision rather than a marketing claim.

Atlassian's newer **Enterprise Certified** program is also a useful target because it evaluates security, reliability, privacy, accessibility and responsible AI—the areas where TestPulse now needs evidence rather than simply more code. citeturn0search9

### What I changed in the V003 plan

The workbook contains **16 findings** and a **14-sprint enhancement programme**, but importantly it does **not** tell Claude to blindly build 14 more feature sprints.

The order is now evidence-first:

**S01 clean-room verification → S02 real Jira LC-1 → S03 Release Quality Intelligence cockpit → S04 design-partner instrumentation → S05 real Marketplace purchase → S06 external security → S07 scale/KVS-vs-SQL → S08 real imports/CI → S09 AI quality → S10 operations → S11 30-day SLO evidence → S12 privacy lifecycle → S13 AEC readiness → S14 launch/kill-continue gate.**

The workbook also includes a **`Claude_Build_Prompt`** sheet ready to copy directly to Claude.

The biggest change from earlier development is: **I would not spend the next cycle adding generic Test Management features.** TestPulse already has enough product surface to test the business hypothesis. Its next major increase in value comes from proving that real Jira teams use its **Release Quality Intelligence** to make release decisions.

That is the point where we find out whether TestPulse is merely a very well-engineered project or a product customers will actually pay for. memcite
